faq: Why not just use a general AI assistant?
For one-off questions, do. A system is for the work that keeps coming back: it's connected to your email, documents and calendar, runs on its own schedule and is built around how you do the job.
Is my job a good fit?

If information arrives all the time, there's a lot to keep track of, or you write the same kind of reply again and again, probably yes. Tell us about it and we'll say plainly whether a system would help.
Do I need to be technical?
No. You tell us how the work happens in your own words. We design it, build it, test it and set it up where you already work.
Where does my information live?
Wherever you're comfortable: on your own computer, in your own accounts, or with a service you choose. We agree on it before anything is built.
Can it do something I didn't want?
Only what you allow. It can be read-only, ask before it sends anything, and keep a record of every change it makes so it can be undone.
What can it connect to?
Whatever your work already runs on: email, texts, calendars, shared folders, spreadsheets, websites and many online services.
Does it have to be an app?
No. It can be a message on your phone each morning, a website, a private dashboard, an iPhone app, or a mix of them.
How much does it do on its own?
As much or as little as you like. Some people want drafts to approve; others want jobs handled start to finish. You choose, and you can change it later.
What does it cost?
It depends on what the system does. Tell us the idea and we'll come back with a plan and a price.
What happens once it's built?
It keeps working for you, and we can keep extending it as your needs change.

qa.title: AI-built. Not AI slop.
qa.lede: Software thrown together with AI has earned a reputation for looking fine and falling apart. Ours goes through strict testing and review before it reaches you, because the experience is the product.
points: Nothing counts as done until it has been run and checked on screen. Passing tests alone don't prove it works.
Reviewers from three different AI companies judge the experience the way a newcomer would: is it clear at a glance, and would you show it to a friend? It doesn't ship without a pass.
Automated tests run against real databases, real browsers and simulated iPhones, and they have to pass before anything ships.
The code is reviewed line by line, the way a careful colleague would, before anything goes out.
When something misses its target, nobody moves the goalposts or calls it close enough. It gets fixed.
Known issues get fixed, not shipped
Anything spotted before launch is fixed first, even small cosmetic things.

steps: Tell us the idea
A sentence is enough: the thing you keep losing track of, the job that eats your evenings, the question you wish you could just ask.
We map how the work happens
Where information arrives, what decisions you make, who else is involved and what a great result looks like to you.
You decide what it handles
What it does on its own, what it checks with you first and how it reaches you. It's your system, set up your way.
We build it and switch it on
You see it working on your real day-to-day, then it grows one piece at a time as your needs do.

story.lede: A real question to our personal system, with the details changed. Nobody told it where to look.
story.ask: When did I get the truck serviced, and what did it all cost?
story.answer: Your truck was serviced on the 14th: one shop receipt and one matching card charge. The parts ordered that same week were for the other car, so I left them out.

Email
Finds the shop's service receipt and the date.
card
Card charges

bag
Orders

chat
Texts
Finds a text thread about fixing someone else's car, and sets those parts aside.
story.kicker: Nobody mentioned the other car. It worked that out on its own.
